hardware: Kaggle, 2 x Tesla T4 (SM75), Python 3.13.16, torch 2.11.0+cu130, Triton 3.6.0, vLLM 0.25.1, attention TRITON_ATTN
scope_note: Notebooks 13 and 14 ran SDK wheel e17b99b4... (bundle manifest efe492a6...). Notebooks 01-12 ran the earlier SDK wheel a6b8596b... with the same vLLM wheel and native binaries; the SDK difference is the replica-routing fix, verified by notebook 14. The released SDK wheel (29edaa55...) differs from the e17b99b4 wheel only in comments, descriptive note strings (identical Python AST ignoring string literals) and the packaged README; it was not itself executed on Kaggle.

fulfilment.tensor_parallel_tp2: VERIFIED: vLLM parallel_config TP=2, both GPUs hold a shard (13751/13751 MiB), deterministic output, memory released
fulfilment.pipeline_parallel_pp2: VERIFIED (experimental): vLLM parallel_config PP=2, both GPUs hold a shard (12895/13353 MiB), deterministic, output equal to TP=1, memory released
fulfilment.replica_parallel: VERIFIED functionally: 50/50 balance checks, both GPUs receive work at batch 2..64 over 3 rounds

performance_conclusion: For Qwen2.5-1.5B (fits one T4) TP=1 is the fastest configuration measured; TP=2 is ~0.55x and PP=2 ~0.6x; two replicas reach 0.91-0.96x of one TP=1 engine up to batch 64. No speed-up from TP, PP or replicas is claimed. TP/PP exist for models that do not fit one 15 GiB T4 (not measured here).
known_limitations: peer access (torch.cuda.can_device_access_peer) differs between Kaggle VMs (true/true in notebook 01, false/false in notebook 07); topology is PHB
notebook 05: vLLM force-killed one TP=2 process at shutdown (memory later released)
notebook 10: host-staged transport and NCCL reference ran with a warning; the custom transport is experimental and is not integrated into vLLM
worker-failure recovery is covered by CPU unit tests only; it was not exercised on Kaggle
no model larger than one T4 was run, so the TP/PP memory-capacity benefit is not demonstrated
L4 / SM89 is not implemented and is not claimed
